title: Creating a More Isogenic Strain of Worms from Parental Strain
author: Cristian Riccio
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.5xwg7pe

steps.title: Isolate single worm onto fresh plates
steps.instruction: Using a bench‑top dissecting light microscope and a Bunsen burner for sterilization, pick a single worm onto a fresh agar NGM plate. Allow it to move away from the point of deposition, then pick the same worm onto a second fresh NGM plate. This two‑step pick ensures no other worms or eggs are co‑picked.

steps.title: Allow worm to populate plate
steps.instruction: Incubate the second plate at the standard growth temperature and let the single worm reproduce until the entire plate is covered with progeny (typically a few days).

steps.title: Chunk full plate and assign strain code
steps.instruction: When the plate is full of worms, cut the agar into two or more chunks and transfer each chunk onto separate fresh plates. Designate the new strain with a lab‑specific code (e.g., SX for the Miska lab). Optionally repeat steps 1 and 2 with the new plates to increase homozygosity.

steps.title: Freeze one derived plate for storage
steps.instruction: Select one of the newly created plates, place it in a cryovial, and freeze it. Use a white plug in one of the five coloured caps on the vial. This frozen vial serves as a permanent stock of the new strain.

steps.title: Bleach and synchronize gravid adults
steps.instruction: Take a plate that is full of gravid adults and treat it with a standard C. elegans bleaching solution to release embryos. Allow the embryos to hatch overnight in M9 buffer, producing arrested L1 larvae (synchronization).

steps.title: Plate L1s and grow to egg‑laying
steps.instruction: Transfer the arrested L1 larvae onto fresh NGM plates and incubate until the worms develop and just begin laying eggs.

steps.title: Bleach newly laid adults and synchronize L1s
steps.instruction: Bleach the plate of synchronized gravid adults that have just started laying eggs to maximize the number of L1s, which survive cryopreservation best. After bleaching, suspend the L1s in 2.5 ml of M9 buffer and let them synchronize overnight.

steps.title: Cryopreserve L1s in multiple tubes
steps.instruction: Verify that the synchronized L1 suspension contains many thrashing larvae. Add 2.5 ml of 2× freezing buffer to the suspension, mix, and aliquot 1 ml into each of five cryopreservation tubes. Place the tubes in a polystyrene box, tape the box shut, and store it at –80 °C (the box slows the temperature drop). The next day, thaw one tube in tap water for 5 min, plate the worms, and confirm viability after a few hours. Email the lab manager, then store one tube in liquid nitrogen for long‑term storage, three tubes in the –80 °C freezer for mid‑term storage, and keep the remaining tube as a backup.
